summary:
Third Eye is an Earth observation intelligence platform that transforms complex satellite data into clear, actionable insights. Built around an interactive 3D globe and map interface, it helps users explore and understand changes happening across Earth.
The project focuses on making NASA Earth observation data, including NISAR radar data, more accessible and useful. Instead of requiring users to interpret complex scientific datasets, Third Eye presents observations and potential events—such as floods, landslides, surface changes, and agricultural changes—in a visual and easy-to-understand way.
A key feature of Third Eye is its AI-powered command interface. Users can interact with the platform using natural language, asking questions or giving commands such as showing potential floods in a specific region. The AI can help users explore data and control parts of the platform through conversation.
Third Eye also includes a learning experience that explains concepts such as radar and Earth observation, helping make satellite science accessible to a wider audience.
Our goal is simple: give people a clearer view of our changing planet and turn powerful Earth observation data into intelligence that people can actually understand and use.
details: Third Eye – Earth Observation Intelligence Platform Third Eye is an Earth observation intelligence platform designed to transform complex satellite data into clear, visual, and actionable insights. Our goal is to make powerful Earth observation technology easier to understand and use—not just for scientists and researchers, but for anyone who wants to explore and understand changes happening on our planet. At the core of Third Eye is an interactive 3D globe and mapping experience that allows users to explore Earth observation data spatially. The platform focuses on using NASA satellite data, including NISAR radar observations, to identify and understand changes on Earth's surface. These changes can help provide insights into events and phenomena such as floods, landslides, changes in land and infrastructure, and agricultural activity. Instead of presenting users with raw scientific datasets that can be difficult to interpret, Third Eye aims to add context and intelligence. Users can explore observations visually, view important details, filter events, analyze changes over time, and better understand the evidence behind an observation. One of the key features of Third Eye is its AI-powered command interface. Users can interact with the platform using natural language, asking questions or giving commands such as, “Show potential floods in Maharashtra” or “Show the biggest event.” The AI is designed to go beyond simply answering questions—it can help control and navigate the platform, making the experience more intuitive and accessible. Third Eye also includes a Learn section and interactive learning experience to help users understand the science behind Earth observation. It introduces concepts such as radar, satellite imaging, and NISAR in simple language, allowing users to explore how the technology works alongside the real-world insights it produces. The project combines satellite science, geospatial visualization, and agentic AI into one platform. Our vision is simple: to give people a clearer, more accessible view of our changing planet and turn powerful Earth observation data into intelligence that people can understand, explore, and act upon.
